question.worked_solution:
Since the logarithms on both sides of the equation have the same base, we can equate the arguments. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{12}⁡({v}^{2}+35) & ={log}_{12}⁡(-12v-1) \\ {v}^{2}+35 & =-12v-1 \\ {v}^{2}+12v+36 & =0 \\ (v+6)^{2} & =0 \\ v & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now check for extraneous solutions by substituting back into the original equation:

- Substituting $v=-6$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{12}⁡({v}^{2}+35) & \overset{?}{=}{log}_{12}⁡(-12v-1) \\ {log}_{12}⁡((-6)^{2}+35) & \overset{?}{=}{log}_{12}⁡(-12(-6)-1) \\ {log}_{12}⁡(71) & ={log}_{12}⁡(71).\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $v=-6$ is a valid solution.
